category_title: Students with severe hearing impairment and EAL who use physical gestures and lip-reading to decipher archaic language
minimal_context: The student is working on a general English classroom task that requires writing a response to a text.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please read the text and write a paragraph about what happens in the story.

STUDENT: (Remains very quiet during the lesson and looks down at the paper without speaking.)

TUTOR: What do you think you will write about?

STUDENT: (Uses very basic verbal communication, saying only a single word, and writes down one sentence.)

TUTOR: Keep trying, please write some more sentences to finish the task.

STUDENT: (Puts the pen down, having written no more than one sentence for the task. He stays very quiet and rarely verbally contributes anything else.)

options.A: Prompt the student to call on a neighbor, ask a friend, or poll the class for help.
options.B: Explain the text in detail, frequently re-explaining the meanings of individual lines and words to the student.
options.C: Give the student stars, stickers, and applause as a reward for completing the writing task.
options.D: Talk to the student alone to make him reflect on the task, asking what makes him feel uncomfortable.
